- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.20) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for first 3 days.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.75) correlate with forecast bias; if sentiment rises after a dip, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
